messages:
mike: Brainstorm: sidecar KMS proxy for Private customers. Need firm answers for auditors about not storing key material or clear key ids. Quick thoughts?
anya: Top constraints: 1) never persist raw key ids, 2) expose only a one-way fingerprint for cross-referencing, 3) strict deny rules for any export/unwrap APIs.
sec-ci: Add automated log scrubber that fails CI if any env contains KEY or KEY_ID at build or if startup logs surface potential key identifiers.
todd: Operationally: fingerprint = sha256(key_identifier || tenant_salt). We keep only the fingerprint. The tenant_salt stays with customer; we allow them to provide proof-of-possession to map events.
rebecca: RBAC minimal roles: kms-proxy-invoker (Encrypt/Decrypt/Sign), kms-proxy-ops (RotateAliases, Disable). Explicit Deny: ExportKey, GetKeyMaterial, ImportKey.
mike: Audit schema proposal: single-line JSON with ts, actor, op, key_fp, trace_id, outcome, proxy_hash. No raw ids anywhere. Example: {"ts":"2026-03-18T14:05:00Z","actor":"svc.billing","op":"Decrypt","key_fp":"sha256:ff...","trace":"rwd-abc","outcome":"ok"}
anya: Incident playbook sketch: detect -> cordon tenant proxies -> collect hashed logs & trace IDs -> ask customer for HSM audit slice -> if confirmed, rotate wrappers and provide signed attestation + chain-of-custody bundle.
sec-ci: On dependency vuln (e.g., PKCS#11 adapter CVE): matrix mapping sidecar builds -> patched versions, emergency patch backport, and compensating sandbox (seccomp / user namespace) while patching. Communicate via standard notification template.
todd: Testing: deterministic fingerprint unit tests, redaction regression tests, integration fake-HSM test ensuring no key material flows through our process, latency test p95 < +10ms.
rebecca: Retention: default 365d enterprise, configurable; consider WORM-backed export option for PCI auditors.
mike: Action items: rebecca -> formal IAM JSON + deny rules; anya -> draft audit schema & FAQ for customers; todd -> seccomp profile + cert pinning doc; sec-ci -> CI tests and redaction checks. I'll drive a short RFC for the sprint. :white_check_mark:
